titleEn: When the First Boat Passes, Wake Up!

pages.text: Toot! A milk boat passed the window. Mom, wearing her headscarf, took the end of the blanket and shook it gently. "Pongi, the first boat is passing. Time to get up." Pongi pulled the blanket right over herself. "Just a little longer..."

Her little brother stood beside the sofa, holding his shell. "Sis! Sis!" Today they were going to look for shells on the bank together. The blanket bundle stayed still as a stone. "I don't want to go out! It's warm here!"
Pongi suddenly sat up on the sofa. The sun was high in the window. The bread on the table was cold, and her little brother was playing with his shell all alone. "Oh! Already?" Pongi's tail drooped.
Mom sat beside the sofa. "Getting up isn't hard at all. When the first boat passes, stretch your body first." Mom took Pongi's paws and stretched them up with her.
Paws out long! Tail out long! Her whole body stretched. Sleepiness slipped away, and even her toes felt light. "Stretching wakes my whole body up! When the first boat passes, wake up!" Pongi called.
Mom whispered behind her. "Now push the window open. Morning is waiting outside." Pongi pushed with both paws. Creak! The window opened little by little.

A breeze blew in. The reeds bent to one side, and the canal water rippled. Pongi spread both paws wide and called, "Hello, morning! When the first boat passes, wake up!" Her little brother raised his shell. "Me!"
One last thing: wash your face! Pongi scooped cold water from the tub and splashed her cheeks. Her face felt fresh and clean. She thumped her tail on the floor. "I started my morning all by myself!"

The next morning, Pongi threw back the blanket and jumped up. "One, stretch when the first boat toots! Two, open the window and say hello to morning! Three, wash your face at the water tub!" Mom stopped in the doorway to watch.

Mom hugged Pongi and patted her back. "You got up before me today, Pongi!" Stretching when the first boat passes sends sleepiness away. "When the first boat passes, wake up! Let's find shells!" Pongi took her brother's paw.
